Foresight value is higher for RTP compared to TOU. The simple average foresight value for eight scenarios (four participation levels, two flexibility types) with the RTP dispatch mechanism is $309/veh-yr, more than 100% higher than the equivalent value of $147/veh-yr for TOU. This is attributable to the increased hourly granularity of RTP. RTP’s increased incentive to schedule EV charging load into specific low-price hours results in difficult-to-serve load spikes. If a perfect forecast of response is used to commit lower-cost generators day-ahead that leads to significantly lower production costs compared to relying on quick start generators to address RTP-induced load spikes in real-time. The less abrupt transitions induced by flattened TOU response are also better managed if first addressed in day-ahead commitment (with perfect foresight), but the difference between doing that and only responding in real-time (no-foresight) is not as pronounced as it is for RTP. 13 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3.3 Week-ahead Hourly Scheduling Maximizes Savings, Presents Implementation Challenges For each participation rate studied, the highest per-vehicle savings is achieved by within-week EVMC actualized using RTP with perfect-foresight or DLC. However, this result might be difficult to implement because wholesale markets do not offer week- ahead schedules or prices, RTP is sensitive to forecast quality, and RTP can produce high ramp rates that must be accommodated by other forms of grid flexibility. Table 4 summarizes which dispatch mechanism provides the most savings with different participation levels and flexibility types. The RTP mechanism with perfect-foresight provides the most production cost savings at low participation rates, and the DLC mechanism provides the most production cost savings at high participation rates. The best-performing mechanism for within-week flexibility outperforms the best-performing mechanism for within-session flexibility. These results suggest an EVMC strategy based on RTP for participation rates less than about 15% of the LDV fleet, DLC for participation rates greater than about 15% the LDV fleet, and scheduling charging over multiple days to a week rather than for single charging sessions.
